answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the quill gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer thus yields nothing, and producing 52 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the tundra ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the walnut review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
